text:
Maria: Quick follow-up from the fp8/int4 RFC — noticed a small but consistent uptick in factual misses on /search/faq canary after switching to the lowbit lane.
Jon: Can you paste a representative example? short snippets often make patterns obvious.
Maria: Heres one (redacted):

S: Q: "What year did X release their v1?"
Baseline: "Released in 2017, see link -> ..."
Lowbit: "I think it was 2016."

Jon: Hmm. That looks like a factual hallucination rather than a formatting or tokenization issue.
Sophie: We talked about per-route precision gating in the RFC but didn't finalize the runtime contract. This seems like a good trigger case.
Ravi: Short summary from telemetry: +0.7% answer-mismatch on /search/faq when precision lane flipped. Problems cluster on short-context Q&A and numeric-heavy tokens.
Alex: That makes sense — our canary evals are biased toward long-form generation. We lack a short-factual gold bucket. :grimacing: 
Maria: Proposal: create a ~200-sample "short-factual" golden set (per-route) used for A/B during canary. Fail criteria: fp8/int4 profile >0.5% absolute degrade vs baseline on that set.
Jon: How do we wire the gating? Two options: live-only telemetry triggers or combined golden + live. Prefer combined to reduce false positives.
Sophie: For live metric, we can compute a lightweight "degradation_score" using a reranker that checks entity overlap and a simple checksum of named entities. Cheap and actionable.
Ravi: We already have per-token surprisal and coverage metrics. I can add delta_surprisal as another signal; mapping that to human quality will need calibration.
Alex: Rollback rule suggestion: require EITHER golden A/B t-test (p < 0.01) OR sustained live delta_rate > threshold for N minutes, but also require minimum sample count and smoothing window.
Maria: Concrete safety params: smoothing window = 10m, min_samples = 500, golden_set_size = 200, golden_threshold = 0.5% degrade. Require both signals for automatic rollback to be conservative (but allow ops to force rollback).
Jon: Runtime needs to expose a "precision_override" / "force_precision" in route config that scheduler and admission honor. Ops-only API with audit log entries. I can add that.
Sophie: Also add a sampling hook to capture (prompt, baseline_resp, new_resp, model, precision_profile) when a fail is detected. Ensure PII scrubbing. This will help root-cause.
Alex: Add a per-route config knob: quality_tolerance: [low, medium, high]. low = strict (<=0.2% degrade), medium = default (<=0.5%), high = permissive (<=1%). Customers or product teams can opt in.
Maria: Action items: 1) Sophie -> seed short-factual eval set with known failures + synthetic numeric Qs (ETA 2d). 2) Ravi -> prototype delta_surprisal metric + smoothing (ETA 4d). 3) Jon -> implement force_precision API + audit logs (ETA 3d). 4) Alex -> add quality_tolerance flag to route config and docs (ETA 2d).
Ravi: I'll drop a minimal telemetry proto with labels: route, precision_profile, delta_surprisal, entity_delta, samples_window.
Sophie: I'll include tests to ensure golden set is deterministic and add fuzzed numeric prompts.
Jon: Runtime note: scheduler will tag requests with precision_profile and emit canary events. On rollback, scheduler switches lane and emits an event. We'll need observability to show which requests hit which lane.
Maria: Also create a short playbook snippet for support: how to read canary events, how to force_precision, and how to collect sampled fails.
ci-bot: Deployed canary-telemetry commit_sha=abc123 to prod-canary at 1770015000 :white_check_mark:
Alex: If we see recurring patterns (e.g., numeric bias), we can recommend a model variant fallback (prefer int8 on numeric-heavy routes) instead of wholesale rollback.
Maria: Goal: preserve >99.5% route-level quality while saving ~20% tokens. Keep gating conservative for the first full rollout.
Jon: I'll update the RFC with these follow-ups after the sync. Thanks, team.
